parsed.attack: A person naturalizes once. The problem stops existing at a specific hour on a specific calendar date the user already knows when they install, typically two to six weeks out, and roughly 90% of interviews are approved - so the entire audience exits permanently, not gradually, and no cohort ever returns. Nothing accumulates for the user either: the 'content library' moat belongs to the vendor, and a transcript of a mock interview for an event that already happened has zero value the next morning. On consumable credits that is not a retention problem, it is an arithmetic one - the author's own kill line puts lifetime revenue under $10 against $20-$80 to acquire, and unlike test prep there is no repeat sitting, no second exam, and no adjacent qualification to sell them.
parsed.strongest_defence: This was never a retention business and should not be judged as one: it is a cram product whose funnel is replenished by roughly 800,000 naturalizations a year, and the community_embed loop moves acquisition onto ESL classes and legal clinics that refer a fresh cohort every term at near-zero marginal CAC, so the institution retains even though no individual does. Adjacent one-off spoken ordeals - citizenship tests in other countries, visa interviews, asylum hearings - reuse the same engine against new cohorts.
parsed.verdict_reason: The revenue model requires repeat purchase from a job that structurally cannot recur - one interview, one lifetime, nothing accumulating - so every dollar of CAC must be repaid inside a single two-week window that ends the same day for every user.
